reply.text:
Here are the cues I'd start with, and if one of them fixes the most, stick with that one.

Set up with the bar over mid-foot, close enough that it nearly touches your shins. Before you pull, take the slack out of the bar: pull up until you feel it click, so your lats are tight and your arms are straight like ropes. Think "push the floor away" rather than "pull the bar up", and keep the bar dragging along your legs the whole way. At the top, stand tall by squeezing your glutes, without leaning back.

The usual mistakes are the bar drifting away from you, hips shooting up before the chest, and rounding your upper back as you yank. Tell me what it feels like is going wrong, for instance the bar swinging forward, hips rising first, or a rounded back, and I'll narrow it to the one cue that matters most.

You can also film a set and I can open the form check for you.
